message.content:
## p7c Rebuild Index Command

```bash
p7c rebuild_index --dry-run --force-lock
```

## Flag Breakdown

| Flag | Short Form | Description |
|------|-----------|-------------|
| `--dry-run` | `-n` | Executes the operation in **simulation mode**. No actual index changes are made to the session table; the command only reports what *would* happen. This is useful for validating the operation before applying it in production. |
| `--force-lock` | `-l` | **Overrides** any existing lock restrictions on the session table and acquires an exclusive lock. Normally, the session table may be locked by other processes or have read-only locks in place. This flag forces acquisition of the lock regardless of current state. |

## What It Does

This command performs the following logical steps:

1. **Acquires an exclusive lock** on the cube session table (forced via `--force-lock`).
2. **Drops the existing index** (simulated in dry-run mode).
3. **Rebuilds the index** on the session table columns (simulated).
4. **Releases the lock** (simulated).

## Example Output (Dry Run)

```
$ p7c rebuild_index --dry-run --force-lock
[INFO] Dry-run mode enabled — no changes will be applied.
[INFO] Acquiring exclusive lock on session table...
[INFO] Lock acquired successfully.
[INFO] Dropping existing index: cube_sessions_idx
[INFO] Rebuilding index: cube_sessions_idx on [session_id, session_hash, created_at]
[INFO] Index would contain 1,428,937 entries.
[INFO] Operation would complete in ~4.2s.
[INFO] Lock released.
[DONE] Dry-run complete. No changes made.
```

## When to Use

- **Pre-production validation** — verify index rebuild logic without risking live session data.
- **Maintenance windows** — the forced lock ensures no other process interferes during the rebuild.
- **Debugging** — inspect lock acquisition behavior and index rebuild performance estimates.

> **Note:** Omitting `--dry-run` will apply the changes live, which requires the session table to have no active sessions and no other process holding a lock on it.
